notes.meaning: The LORD gives Ezekiel a new message about a future attack on God's people. Even though Israel will return home from exile, God warns them beforehand that hard trials still lie ahead. Believers can take comfort knowing that God sees every future danger before it ever happens.

God tells Ezekiel to speak directly against Gog, the ruler over Magog, Meshech, and Tubal. The LORD declares that He is against this proud leader and will stand in his way. No earthly ruler, no matter how mighty or confident, can match the power of God.

differ.view: Many understand Gog and his armies as a symbolic picture of all worldly hostility against the church rather than a literal future coalition of specific nations.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic interpreters often understand Gog as a figure representing worldly persecutors of the church throughout history, or the final Antichrist near the end of time.

notes.meaning: God says He will turn Gog around like a captive beast, putting hooks in his jaws to march him out. The invader will bring an enormous army filled with horses, horsemen, and weapons of war. Gog will think he is following his own desires, but God is drawing him toward his own defeat.

A massive coalition of armies from distant lands will join Gog in his campaign. These forces include Persia from the east, Cush and Put from Africa, and Gomer and Beth-togarmah from the far north. Together, they represent an alliance that gathers from every direction against the people of God.

The LORD uses mocking words to tell Gog to get ready and take command of all his allied troops. Gog can gather every weapon and rally all his soldiers, but his preparations will be useless. Even the greatest army cannot stand when God opposes it.

Long after the exile, Gog will be summoned to march against the land of Israel. Its people will have been gathered back from many nations to live in peace on mountains that once lay in ruins. The invasion targets a people who believe they are resting securely under God's care.

differ.view: Many understand this as a literal invasion of the modern nation of Israel that will take place in the end times.

notes.meaning: Gog and his massive horde will rush into the land like a sudden thunderstorm. Their numbers will be so great that they cover the hills and valleys like a dark cloud. This terrifying sight will make it look as though Israel has no hope of survival.

When the time comes, a wicked thought will enter Gog's mind, and he will hatch an evil scheme. God permits this raid, but Gog chooses it out of his own greed and cruelty. God knows the secret plans of human hearts long before they are carried out.

Gog plans to raid a peaceful people who live without city walls, gates, or bars for defense. He wants to plunder their silver, gold, cattle, and goods now that they have resettled at the center of the land. Because the people seem weak and helpless, he expects an easy victory.

Merchant nations like Sheba, Dedan, and the traders of Tarshish ask Gog if he has come only to steal wealth and livestock. These traders do not fight in the war themselves, but they hope to profit by buying and selling the stolen goods. Worldly greed makes them eager to gain from the suffering of others.

God commands Ezekiel to warn Gog that Israel's peaceful way of life will catch his attention. The invader will see that God's people live without fear and will take that peace as a chance to attack. Gog fails to understand that Israel's true protection comes from the LORD Himself.

Gog will sweep down from the far north with a huge army of horsemen, covering the land like a storm cloud. God Himself will bring this enemy against His land in the latter days to accomplish His own purpose. When the LORD destroys this mighty force, the watching nations will clearly see His holiness.

The LORD asks Gog if he is the very attacker spoken of by Israel's earlier prophets. Long before Ezekiel's day, God's servants warned that a final enemy would come against His chosen people. God's ancient warnings prove that nothing in this battle takes Him by surprise.

As soon as Gog steps foot on Israel's soil, God's burning fury will rise up. The LORD has shown great patience, but an attack on His restored people will trigger His righteous anger. God will personally step in to defend those who belong to Him.

In His fierce zeal, the LORD declares that a massive earthquake will shake the entire land of Israel. This violent shaking will show everyone that the living God has arrived to fight. No human army can hold its ground when the earth itself trembles before the Creator.

Every creature in the sea, the sky, and the fields, along with all human beings, will shake with fear before God. Mountain ridges will be torn down, steep cliffs will collapse, and every defensive wall will fall. All human strength and natural barriers will prove completely useless against the LORD.

God will summon a sword against Gog across all the mountains of Israel. He will send such deep confusion through the invading forces that every soldier will turn his weapon on his fellow soldier. God often brings down the wicked by turning their own violence back upon themselves.

The LORD will punish Gog and his allied troops with deadly disease, torrential rain, hailstones, and burning sulfur. These terrifying judgments recall the destruction of Sodom and the plagues sent on ancient Egypt. God uses the full force of creation to crush the forces of evil.

Through this complete victory, God will show His greatness and holiness before many nations. The defeat of this vast coalition will leave no doubt about who is in charge. People from all over the world will finally recognize that He alone is the LORD.
